THEY EXPECTED FLAT SEAFLOOR — INSTEAD, THEY FOUND THIS 
At 3.4 miles beneath the Pacific Ocean, scientists expected to find a mostly flat abyssal plain.

But the ROV revealed something completely different.

Large volcanic boulders, pillow lavas and rugged terrain covered the seafloor—more like a hidden underwater mountain landscape than a flat plain.

And growing among the rocks was a 5.3-foot bamboo whip coral that may represent a depth record for its type.

🌊 How many hidden landscapes are still waiting beneath the ocean?

PARTS OF THIS PACIFIC ARE STILL UNMAPPED 

Scientists are heading into one of the least-understood parts of the Pacific.

A new expedition launched this week to explore previously unmapped seamounts, underwater ridges and abyssal plains around Hawaiʻi.

Using powerful sonar and remotely operated vehicles, researchers will investigate terrain that has barely been observed directly.

And that creates the real mystery…

What is living—and what is hiding—on these underwater mountains?

The exploration is underway now.

🌊 Would you watch a live dive into a place humans have barely seen?
